recall.minute: Linear regression predicts $y$ as $\theta^\top x$. We pick θ by minimising the mean squared error $J(\theta)$, a convex bowl. Either solve it directly with the normal equation $(X^\top X)^{-1}X^\top y$, which is exact but costly with many features, or walk downhill with gradient descent, $\theta\leftarrow\theta-\alpha\nabla J$, choosing α carefully and scaling features. Batch, mini-batch and stochastic GD trade stability for speed. Judge fits with MAE, RMSE and $R^2$ on unseen data. Basis functions let a linear model fit curves, which risks overfitting; counter it with more data, simpler models, early stopping or regularisation: Ridge shrinks weights, Lasso zeroes some, Elastic Net mixes both.
